subtopics.title: Network Application Architectures
subtopics.summary: Contrast client-server architectures (data centers, always-on servers) with P2P architectures (self-scalability, minimal server infrastructure) and hybrid designs, including examples like Web, e-mail, and file sharing.

subtopics.title: Processes Communicating
subtopics.summary: Explain how processes on different end systems communicate: client vs. server processes, the socket as the interface between an application process and the transport layer, and addressing a destination process via IP address and port number.

subtopics.title: Transport Services Available to Applications
subtopics.summary: Identify the four classes of service an application may need from a transport layer: reliable data transfer, throughput guarantees, timing guarantees, and security.

subtopics.title: Transport Services Provided by the Internet
subtopics.summary: Describe the TCP service model (connection-oriented, reliable, congestion control) versus the UDP service model (connectionless, unreliable, minimal), and note why neither provides throughput, timing, or security guarantees (motivating SSL/TLS).

subtopics.title: Application-Layer Protocols
subtopics.summary: Define what an application-layer protocol specifies—message types, message syntax, field semantics, and rules for when/how processes send and respond to messages—and distinguish open protocols (e.g., HTTP, SMTP) from proprietary ones.
